lines.en: An epistle published by the famous and holy emperor

lines.text: τοῦ Πορφυρογεννήτου κυροῦ Μανουὴλ τοῦ Κομνηνοῦ,
γέμουσα πολλῶν καὶ ὑψηλῶν καὶ ἀναγκαίων θεωρημά-
lines.en: full of many and lofty and necessary theorems,

lines.text: των, ἀπολογητικὴ πρὸς γραφήν τινος μοναχοῦ παλατί-
lines.en: apologetic against a writing of a certain palatine monk

lines.text: νου τῆς μονῆς τοῦ Παντοκράτορος τὰ τῆς ἀστρονομι-
lines.en: of the monastery of the Pantokrator, which criticized the things of the astronomical

lines.text: κῆς τέχνης κακίζουσαν καὶ ἀσέβειαν ἀποκαλοῦσαν τὸ

lines.text: Τιμιώτατε πάτερ, τὸ ἐγχειρισθὲν τῇ βασιλείᾳ μου γράμμα σου
lines.en: Most honorable father, your letter handed to my majesty

lines.text: ὑπανεγνώσθη μοι αὐτίκα καταδρομὴν περιέχον τοῦ τῆς ἀστρονομίας
lines.en: was read to me immediately, containing an attack on the discipline of astronomy

lines.text: μαθήματος ἀπὸ χρήσεων γραφικῶν συγκροτούμενον, καθώσπερ ἐδό-
lines.en: composed from scriptural uses, just as it seemed

lines.text: κει σοι. ἦν μὲν οὖν τὸ γράμμα ἐπάξιον ἁπλότητος μοναχοῦ, ὅμως
lines.en: to you. The letter was indeed worthy of the simplicity of a monk, nevertheless

lines.text: μέντοι οὐκ ἐσκεμμένως καὶ λογίως γραφὲν ἀλλ’ ἀνεπιστημόνως πάντη
lines.en: however not written deliberately and learnedly but altogether unscientifically

lines.en: and outside of accuracy, so that neither partaking of outside learning from it

lines.en: is the one who wrote it shown, nor indeed of our and holy and

sections.text: 12 ἐσκεμένως A(ngelicus). 14 τῶν καθ’ ἡμᾶς V(enetus). An ἡμᾶς Γραφῆς ἁγίας? cf. p. 112, 2.
sections.en: 12 ἐσκεμένως ('deliberately') A(ngelicus). 14 τῶν καθ’ ἡμᾶς ('of those according to us') V(enetus). Or ἡμᾶς Γραφῆς ἁγίας ('us of the Holy Scripture')? cf. p. 112, 2.

sections.text: 1 De illis libris, cf. Krumbacher Sitzungsb. Akad. München, 1894, p. 399 s. Codi- cem Ω 104 s. XVI monasterii Lavra in monte Atho quadraginta septem epistulas Glycae continere nos monet Daniel Serruys, quarum ultima est Ἀνταπολογητικόν.
sections.en: 1 Concerning those books, cf. Krumbacher Sitzungsb. Akad. München, 1894, p. 399 s. Daniel Serruys advises us that Codex Ω 104 s. XVI of the Lavra monastery on Mount Athos contains forty-seven letters of Glycas, of which the last is the Ἀνταπολογητικόν ('Counter-apology').

sections.text:
Manuelis Comneni opusculum descripsi partim ex ipso codice Romano partim
ex imaginibus photographicis quas concedente bibliothecae Angelicae praefecto
conficiendas curavi. Doctissimus iuvenis Daniel Serruys, cui gratias ago maximas,
apographon quoque pp. 113, 4 - 115, 8 et 117, 10 - 118, 10 comiter mecum commu-
nicavit, ita ut duplici labore verissimam Angelici libri effigiem habeamus. —
Codicis Veneti (Marcian. 324, s. XV, f. 312, cf. Catal., II, p. 15), exemplar quod
summa cura confecerat, liberalissime utendum mihi concedit Josephus Laurent,
professor Nanceiensis. Quo beneficio valde nos devinxit, nam effecit ut plura verba
in Angelico omissa supplere vel depravata sanare potuerimus. Aliae vero lacunae
vel corruptelae utrique codici sunt communes, qui manifeste ambo ex eodem
archetypo descripti sunt. Plura enim a librario consulto suppressa sunt, cf. ad
p. 111, 23, 128, 27. — Codicem Vaticanum 1059 qui idém Manuelis opusculum
continet (Krumbacher, Byz. Lit. 2, p. 627) conferre nobis non contigit.
sections.en:
I have transcribed the short work of Manuel Comnenus partly from the Roman codex itself, partly
from photographic images which, with the permission of the prefect of the Angelica library,
I saw to being made. The most learned young man Daniel Serruys, to whom I give the greatest thanks,
also kindly shared with me a copy of pp. 113, 4 - 115, 8 and 117, 10 - 118, 10,
so that by a double labor we have the truest image of the Angelican book. —
Josephus Laurent, professor at Nancy, most generously grants me the use of a copy of the Venetian codex
(Marcian. 324, s. XV, f. 312, cf. Catal., II, p. 15), which he had made with the greatest care.
By this kindness he has greatly obliged us, for he brought it about that we could supply many words
omitted in the Angelicus or heal corrupted ones. But other lacunae
or corruptions are common to both codices, which clearly were both copied from the same
archetype. For many things were deliberately suppressed by the scribe, cf. at
p. 111, 23, 128, 27. — It did not fall to us to collate the Vatican codex 1059 which contains the same short work of Manuel
(Krumbacher, Byz. Lit. 2, p. 627).

sections.text:
Inter complures libros qui Glycae epistulas praehent 1 tres nobis praesto fuerunt.
Intercedente Francisco Boll diligentissimus iuvenis Paulus Marc codicem Monacen-
sem 415, f. 217 ss., saec. XV accurate nobis descripsit. Cum hoc exemplari cod. Pari-
sinum 228, saec. XIII, f. 95 ss., ipse contuli. Etiam codicem Taurinensem CXCIII,
f. 154 ss., saec. XV ineuntis, nunc acerrimo casu forsan combustum adhibui, qui
textum praebebat decurtatum, nam epistula fine mutila erat (v. p. 125). F. C.
sections.en:
Among the several books which offer the letters of Glycas 1 three were available to us.
Through the intervention of Franciscus Boll the most diligent young man Paulus Marc accurately transcribed for us the Munich codex
415, f. 217 ss., saec. XV. With this copy I myself collated the Parisian codex
228, saec. XIII, f. 95 ss. I also used the Turin codex CXCIII,
f. 154 ss., of the beginning of the 15th century, now perhaps burned by a most bitter chance, which
offered a truncated text, for the letter was mutilated at the end (see p. 125). [F. C.]

summary.headline: Manuel Komnenos Defends Astronomy
summary.text: Opening of Manuel Komnenos’s apologetic epistle defending astronomy against a Pantokrator monk’s scriptural attack on the discipline, followed by the editor’s account of manuscripts used: Angelicus, Venetian Marcianus 324, Vaticanus 1059, and codices bearing Glycas’s letters.
